intro.author: Mostly Solomon (1:1; 10:1; 25:1), with sections from 'the wise' (22:17; 24:23), Agur son of Jakeh (30:1) and King Lemuel, who records his mother's teaching (31:1)
intro.written: Solomon reigned about 970–930 BC; King Hezekiah's scribes copied more of his proverbs around 700 BC (25:1). Many scholars think the book reached its final form later still.
intro.audience: Young people in Israel, addressed as 'my son', and anyone willing to learn, from the simple to the already wise (1:4-5)
intro.setting: Collections of practical teaching were common across the ancient world, especially in Egypt, where officials trained young men for public life. Solomon was famous for this kind of wisdom (1 Kings 4:29-34). Israel's sages gathered sayings about work, money, speech, family and justice, and rooted them all in reverence for the Lord.
intro.purpose: To give the simple good sense and the young knowledge and discretion (1:2-6), training them to live skillfully in God's world.
intro.bigIdea: Real wisdom begins with the fear of the Lord and shows up in ordinary choices: words, work, money, friendships and family.
